LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT 1976

LICENSING OF TRADES, BUSINESSES AND INDUSTRIES
(FEDERAL TERRITORY OF LABUAN) BY-LAWS 2016

IN exercise of the power conferred by paragraph 102(s) of the
Local Government Act 1976 [ Act 171 ] (as extended and modified by the
Federal Territory of Labuan (Extension and Modification of Local Government
Act 1976) Ord er 2010 [ P.U. (A) 439/2010 ]), the Perbadanan Labuan  makes,
and pursuant to section 103 of the Act, the Minister confirms, the following by-laws:

PART I
PRELIMINARY

Citation and commencement
1. (1) These by-laws may be cited a s the Licensing of Trades, Businesses and
Industries (Federal Territory of Labuan) By-Laws 2016.

(2) These By-laws come into operation on 1 September 2016.

Interpretation
2. In these By-laws, unless the context otherwise requires—

"business activity" means any trade, business or industrial activity as specified in
the Schedule;

"licence fee" means the prescribed payment rate for a licence issued under these
By-laws as specified in the Schedule;

"private higher ed ucational institution" shall have  the same meaning as defined
in the Private Higher Educational Institutions Act 1996 [Act 555];

"licensee" means any person to whom a business premise licence is issued
under these By-laws for the purpose of operating a business activity as prescribed in the
Schedule;

"Perbadanan" means the Perbadanan Labuan established under section 3 of the
Perbadanan Labuan Act 2001 [Act 609];

"premise" shall have  the same meaning as defined in the Street, Drainage and
Building Act 1974 [ Act 133 ] (as extend ed and modified by the Federal Territory of
Labuan (Extension and Modification of Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974)
Order 2010 [P.U. (A) 394/2010]);

"private healthcare facilities and s ervices" shall have  the same meaning
as defined in the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 [Act 586];

"business premise" means a premise which is used to operate a business activity;
and

"private school" or "private educational institution" shall have the same  meaning
as defined in the Education Act 1996 [Act 550].

PART II
LICENSING

Licence required for business activity
3. (1) Any person may use any premise for operating any business activity when
a planning approval, if necessary, for that purpose has been obtained under the relevant
planning law and a business premise licence has been issued pertaining to the said
premise by the Perbadanan under these By-laws.

(2) Any person who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Application for a licence
4. (1) Subject to by-law 3, an applicatio n for a licence under these By -laws shall
be made in such form and manner as determined by the Perbadanan.

(2) The Perbadanan may approve or not approve an application for  a licence
under these By-laws.

(3) The Perbadanan may, if the Perbadanan  thinks necessary, require any
applicant to attend in person or  on behalf of a corporation or firm, or a representative
authorised by the corporation or firm to attend  to furnish any  document or further
information regarding an application for a licence.

(4) A licence issued under these By-laws shall be subject to—

(a) the licence period as determined by the Perbadanan;

(b) the suitability and the size of the premise to be used to operate the
proposed business activity;

(c) the pr ovisions of these By -laws, conditions and restrictions
imposed by the Perbadanan and by any relevant authorities;

(d) payment of deposit as provided in by-law 8;

(e) payment of a licence fee as prescribed in the Schedule; and

(f) any other requirements under any relevant laws.

(5)       The Perbadanan may, from time to time and while a licence is still in force,
impose any additional conditions on the licence or amend or revoke any condition
imposed on the licence.

(6)       A written notice shall be g iven to the licensee before the Perbadanan
makes any decision under paragraph (5).

Disqualification
5. Notwithstanding by-law 4, no lice nce shall be issued under these By-laws to any
person—

(a) under the age of eighteen years old; or

(b) if the premise  proposed by him, in the opinion of the Perbadanan, is not
suitable to be used as a business premise or the proposed premise is
located in an area which is not suitable for operating the proposed
business activity.

Form of licence
6. A licence issued unde r these By-laws shall be in any form as may be determined
by the Perbadanan.

Licence fee
7. (1) The licence fee payable for the issuance of a licence under these By -laws
is as prescribed in the Schedule.

(2) The Perbadanan may  exempt any licensee from th e responsibility of
paying the whole or any part of the licence fee.

(3) The licence fee paid under paragraph (1) shall not be refundable.

Deposit
8. (1) The Perbadanan may require any person to whom a licence is issued to
pay a deposit of an amount of money not exceeding fifty thousand ringgit to ensure that
the provisions of the Act, By-laws, conditions or restrictions of the licence are observed.

(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Perbadanan may exempt any licensee
from the responsibility of paying the whole or any part of the deposit.

(3)  If there is a breach of any of the provisions of the Act, By-laws, conditions
or restrictions of the licence, the Perbadanan shall give notice to the licensee within
the time specified in the noti ce to give representation as to why his deposit shall not be
forfeited.

(4) The Perbadanan may, after considering the representation given by the
licensee or if the licensee fails to make a representation , decides either to forfeit the
whole or part of the deposit.

(5) Subject to  paragraph (4), the Perbadanan may require the licensee to
replace the whole or part of the deposit that has been forfeited.

(6) The deposit paid shall, unless forfeited, be refunded to the licensee
without any adjustment for interest on the amount deposited under paragraph (1) after
the licensee has ceased operating the business activity.

(7) The licensee shall inform the Perbadanan if he has ceased operating
the business activity.

(8) Notwithstanding paragraph (7), the licensee shall apply to the
Perbadanan within thirty days from the date he has ceased operating the business
activity for his deposit to be refunded.

(9) If the licensee does not apply for his deposit to be refunded or the deposit
is not claimed within the period specified under paragraph (8) , the deposit shall be
forfeited and shall be paid into the Perbadanan Labuan Fund  and shall form p art of the
revenue of the fund.

Replacement licence
9. If the Perbadanan is satisfied that a  valid licence issued under these By -laws is
lost, defaced or damaged, the Perbadanan may issue a replacement licence.

Transfer of licence
10. (1) The licensee may submit an application to t ransfer the licence to any
party in such form as dete rmined by the Perbadanan and the Perbadanan may approve
or refuse such application.

(2) The fee for the transfer of the licence shall be twenty five ringgit.

(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if there is a change of entity or change of
name in the entit y, the licensee shall forward a copy of the certification of the change
from the Companies Commission of Malaysia.

Renewal of licence
11. (1) A licence issued under these By -laws shall not be renewed as a right and
an application for renewal of licence shall be deemed as an application for a licence.

(2) An application for renewal of a licence shall be made within sixty days
before the expiry of the licence and shall be made in such form and manner as may be
determined by the Perbadanan.

(3) The Perbadanan may, if the Perbadanan thinks necessary, require any
applicant to attend in person or on behalf of a corporation or firm, or a representative
authorised by the corporation or firm to attend to furnish any document or further
information regarding an application to renew a licence.

(4) The Perbadanan may renew or not renew a licence and shall inform the
applicant of his decision in writing or by any other manner as may be determined by the
Perbadanan and to refund the deposit to the applicant subject to by-law 8(9).

(5) A licence if renewed under paragraph (4) shall be subject to—

(a) the licence period as determined by the Perbadanan;

(b) payment of a licence fee as prescribed in the Schedule; and

(c) the provisions of these By -laws, conditions and re strictions
imposed by the Perbadanan and by any relevant authorities.

(6) No further deposit needs to be given by the licen see if his licence is
renewed.

(7) The Perbadanan shall not be responsible to pay any compensation to the
licensee if the licence is not renewed under paragraph (4).

Revocation of licence
12. (1) The Perbadanan may revoke a licence issued under  by-law 4 if the
Perbadanan is satisfied that—

(a) the licensee has contravened any pr ovisions of the  Act, By -laws,
conditions or restrictions of the licence;

(b) the licensee has, either in relation to the application of a licence or
at any time after the licence is issued, submitted to the
Perbadanan, a document or declaration which is false, confusing or
not accurate;

(c) the licensee has not operated the licensed business activity  for a
consecutive period of three months without informing the
Perbadanan; or

(d)  a winding up order or bankruptcy order was made against the
licensee or a resolution for volunta ry winding up has been
approved.

(2) Revocation of licence under  paragraph (1) may be made by the
Perbadanan without any payment of  compensation to the licensee and the Perbadanan
may forfeit the whole deposit paid under by-law 8.

(3) Before the revocation of a licence, the Perbadanan shall give a notice in
writing to the licensee requiring him to make a representation within the period as
specified in the notice as to why his licence shall not be revoked.

(4) (a) After the expiry of the perio d specified in the notice under
paragraph (3) and after considering the licensee's representation or if the licensee fails
to make a representation, the Perbadanan shall proceed to consider such matter and
inform his decision in a written notice to the licensee.

(b) If the Perbadanan decides to re voke the licence, the revocation of
the licence shall take effect on the date specified in the notice served to the licensee.

(5) Any licensee who operates a business activity after his licence is revoked
under paragraph (4) commits an offence.

PART III
SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR TIMBER STORE

Prohibition of burning of sawdust and timber waste
13. (1) The licensee shall not permit any person to burn sawdust or timber waste
within his timber store area  unless permitted by the Perbadanan subject to any
conditions as the Perbadanan thinks necessary.

(2) The licensee shall ensure that the cut timber in the timber store is stored
and staked in a tidy and orderly  manner to the Perbadanan 's satisfaction and in such
manner that does not obstruct an entrance, exit or passageway.

(3) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an offence.

PART IV
SPECIAL PROVISION FOR LAUNDRY

Definition
14. For the purpose of this Part, unless the context otherwise requires—

"laundry" means any  business premise providing service for washing or ironing
of clothes commercially , either manually, mechanically, using steam, dry cleaning or in
any other manner; and

"clothes" includes clothing, towels, linen, rugs, cushion covers, table cloth s,
blankets, pillow covers, bedshe ets, curtains or any other washable items made from
woven material.

Wall and floor specifications
15. (1) The walls of the laundry where washing i s done manually shall be fixed
with glazed tiles or water resistant material to a height of not less than two metres
unless exempted by the Perbadanan.

(2) The floor of the laundry where washing is carried out shall be made of
smooth impervious material and graded so that all fluids are flowing and not stagnant in
the wash area.

(3) Any laundry li censee who cont ravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an
offence.

Special requirements for laundry
16. (1) The laundry licensee shall ensure that—

(a) washed clothes are separated from dirty clothes and shall be kept
on shelves, tables, in containers, or in a suitable storage;

(b) all utensils, equipments, fittings and machinery in his business
premise be kept in a clean condition at all times; and

(c) washed clothes  are not to be dried on the ground and shall be
dried on clothes lines or at a specific place for dryi ng clothes
within his business premise area.

(2) Any laundry licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Prohibition of lending out clothes
17. (1) No laundry licensee shall use, lend or hire out any clothes entrusted to
him to be washed or ironed.

(2) Any laundry licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

PART V
SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR BEAUTY AND HEALTH CARE CENTRE

Definition
18. For the purpose of this Part, unless the context otherwise requires—

"cosmetic" means any substance used fo r treating or maintaining the
complexion, skin or hair, and includes toiletries;

"hairdressing'' means hair removal or  transplant, haircutting, hairwaving,
trimming, dyeing, shaving, shampooing and every similar operation usually performed
by a hairdresse r either manually, mechanically, electrically or by means of any powder
or solution or by any combination of such methods;

"beauty and health care centre" means—

(i) any business premise used to provide beauty treatment or health care but
does not include a hospital or a clinic at where  patients are treated under

the supervision of a medical practitioner registered under the
Medical Act 1971  [Act 50], an infirmary,  a nursing or convalescent home
or any other  similar premises providing the following services or any
combination of the following services:

(a) facial treatment;

(b) manicure and pedicure;

(c) waxing;

(d) hairdressing;

(e) tattoo;

(f) application of cosmetics or beautifying;

(g) body slimming;

(h) herbs, milk and flower bath;

(i) body scrub; or

(j) any ot her activit ies as may be determined by the Perbadanan as
beauty and health care treatment;

(ii) any business premise used to provide massage, physical fitness treatment
or exercise with or without equipment providing the following services or
any combination of the following services:

(1) massage:
(a) traditional massage;
(b) handicapped massage;

(c) reflexology;
(d) aromatherapy;
(e) modern massage using any equipments;
(f) physiotherapy;
(g) acupuncture; or
(h) bekam;

(2) sauna/spa and jacuzzi;

(3) aerobic/fitness centre/gymnasium;

(4) meditation centre; or

(5) any other health treatment permitted by the Perbadanan.

"treatment" means  any beauty treatment, facial treatment, manicure and
pedicure, hairdressing, steam bath  or any other special bath, chiropody ,
electrical treat ment, body slimming or any other similar treatment or physical fitness
exercise with or without equipment;

"herbal remedy" means any treatment usin g herbal substance s or a mixture of
herbal substance produced by the process of drying, crushing or comminut ing,
but without involving any other process, a natural substance or sub stances of plant  or
mineral origin or any other part of such substance or substances; and

"beauty treatment" means any treatment by application  of cosmetics or herb al
remedy on the  body or any part of the body, face or hair for treating or improving the
complexion of the body  or face, body slimming, facial massage, hairdressing,
manicure and pedicure, sauna or herbal bath and spa but does not inclu de any form of
plastic surgery.

Prohibition on full partitioning of beauty and health care centre
19. (1) The licensee shall not fully partition or permit to be fully partitioned the
space or use tinted glass in the business premise used for beauty and health care centre.

(2) The licensee may, in the space used for  beauty treatment, use a curtain or
screen made of any material determined by the Perbadanan to separate the beds use d
for providing beauty  treatment but such curtain or screen shall not exceed t wo metres
in height from the floor.

(3) The surface of t he d oor of the area where  beauty treatment is  rendered
shall be one -fourth covered by transparent glass and the door shall be kept unfastened
during the business hours.

(4) Any licensee who contravenes this by-law commits an offence.

PART VI
GENERAL PROVISIONS

Prohibitions
20. (1) No licensee shall—

(a) employ any person who is under the age of eighteen years;

(b) employ any foreigner without a valid work permit to work in his
business premise;

(c) allow an y gam bling or immo ral activit ies or allow any conduct
which will cause nuisance, disturbance, injury or noisiness to the
residents within the surrounding area of his business premise;

(d) allow any animal to remain in his business premise other than the
premise operating a business or providing a service relating to
animals; and

(e) carry out other activities  in his business premise other than the
business activity specified in his licence.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Medical examination
21. (1) The Perbadanan may at any time, if the Perbadanan  thinks necessary,
instruct the licensee and his employees to undergo  a medical examination by a medical
or health officer registered under the Medical Act 1971 [Act 50].

(2) Any lic ensee who fails to comply  with the instruction issued under
paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Register of employees
22. (1) The licensee shall provide a register book containing the name, identity
card number, passport number and a valid work permit of no n-citizen employee s,
recent residential address, qualification, photograph and any other relevant particulars
of his employees and shall produce the register book for inspection whenever required
by the Perbadanan.

(2) Any licensee who fails to comply with paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Sanitary requirements and maintenance of the business premise
23. (1) The licensee shall—

(a) ensure that all mechanical or electrical equipment which is used in
his business premise is maintained in a good condition and safe to
be used at all times;

(b) keep all areas, forecourts and open spaces forming part of his
business premise to be in a clean condition;

(c) provide sufficient refuse bins in his business premise; and

(d) provide sufficient toilet facilities and  ensure that the toilet is in a
clean condition at all times.

(2) Any licensee who fails to comply with paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Disposal of refuse
24. All refuse related to the business activity  shall be placed in plastic bags or
any other suitable containers before being deposited into refuse bins or receptacles and
shall be disposed of in such manner as may be determined by the Perbadanan or by any
agency responsible for such matter.

Spilling of noxious liquid or refuse
25. (1) No licensee shall cause any noxious liquid or refuse relating to his
business activity to be thrown, discarded, spilled, left or scattered in any public place.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

(3) For the purpose of this  by-law, " public place" shall have the meaning
as defined in section 2 of the Local Government Act 1976 [ Act 171]
(as extended and modified by the Federal Territory of Labuan (Extension and
Modification of Local Government Act 1976) Order 2010 [P.U. (A) 439/2010]).

Ventilation and lighting
26. (1) The licensee shall ensure that—

(a) there is sufficient and suitable lighting in his business premise;

(b) there is sufficient ventilation in his business premise; and

(c) every staircase, passage, exit and emergency exit forming part of
his business premise is provided with sufficient lighting.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Crowded space is prohibited
27. (1) The licensee shall ensure that his  business premise is not crowded with
any furniture,  things or goods  relating to his business activity  which may affect
the safety, health or cause nuisance to any person in the business premise.

(2) If in the  opinion of the Perbadanan a business premise is in a crowded
situation, the Perbadanan may by notice in writing direct the licensee within the period
specified in the notice to re arrange the furniture,  things or goods within the business
premise until the Perbadanan is satisfied that the business premise is no longer in a
crowded situation.

(3) Any licensee who fails to comp ly with the notice issued under paragraph
(2) commits an offence.

(4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3 ), any licensee who fails to compl y with
paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Firefighting equipment, staircases, exits and doors
28. (1) The licensee shall ensure that—

(a)  there is sufficient fire fighting equipment approved by the relevant
authorities installed in his business premise and in a working
condition; and

(b)  all staircases, passages, landings and exits if forming part of the
business premise are maint ained in good order and clear from
obstruction and every door in the business premise is constructed
and fitted as to be readily opened at all times.

(2) The Perbadanan may, by notice in writing , instructs the licensee  to carry
out the requirements under paragraph (1) within the period specified in the notice.

(3) Any licensee who fails to comply with t he notice issued under pa ragraph
(2) commits an offence.

(4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), any licensee who contravenes paragraph
(1) commits an offence.

Inflammable substances
29. (1) Cement or any i nflammable solution sh all be kept in  closed containers of
approved design by the Perbadanan.

(2) Where solvents, solutions or cement having a flash point below 23ºC
are kept in quantities exceeding 45 litres, a non -flammable store shall be constructed
according to the requirements of the Perbadanan.

(3) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an offence.

Storage
30. (1) All materials shall be stored in such manner and state as to prevent the
emission of noxious or offensive effluent therefrom.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Burning
31. (1) The licensee shall not burn or cause to be burnt refuse or materials or
other waste in relation  to his business activity  except in such manner and at a place
approved by the Perbadanan.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Effluent
32. (1) The licensee shall not discharge or cause or permit to be discharged any
effluent except scheduled effluent which complies with the limit of discharge as
prescribed under the Environmental Quality (Sewage) Reg ulations 2009

[P.U. (A) 432/2009] and the Environmental Quality (Control of Pollution From Solid
Waste Transfer Station and Landfill) Regulations 2009 [ P.U. (A) 433/2009), at a place or
places as specified by the Perbadanan to discharge effluent and app roved in writing
by the Director General of the Department of Environment.

(2) For the purpose of paragraph (1), "effluent" shall have the meaning given
to it under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 [ Act 127 ] and re gulations made
thereunder.

Spreading of dust, etc.
33. (1) The licensee shall not cause, let, allow or permit any spreading of dust,
fume, vapour, gas heat, radiation, odour, smell, vibration, smoke or soot from his
business premise which in the opinion o f the Perbadanan is a nuisance or whi ch may
cause air pollution.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Nuisance
34. (1) The licen see shall not, during  the operation of  his business activity ,
create or cause or allow any nuisance to occur.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Operating hours for business activity
35. (1) The Perbadanan may direct a business activity  to be operated in the
business premise within the period and time as specified by the Perbadanan and
the licensee shall comply with such direction.

(2) The Perbadanan may consider an application from the licensee to extend
the period and time specified by the Perbadanan under paragraph (1) upon receiving
an application in writing from the licensee.

(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), any licensee who contravenes paragraph
(1) commits an offence.

Power to enter premise for inspection purposes
36. The Perbadanan may—

(a) enter and inspect any  business premise used or which the Perbadanan
suspects with reasonable cause is being use d to operate  any business
activity for which a licence is required under these By-laws;

(b) request from the licensee any information regarding the management of
the business premise and the licensee or his employee shall provide any
information required from him.

Exemption
37. The Perbadanan may, conditionally or unconditionally exempt any licensee from
any provisions of these By-laws.

Penalty
38. Any person who contravenes any prov ision of these By -laws shall be guilty of
an offence and shall , upon conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding two thousand
ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year or to both , and in the case
of a continuing offence, to a fine not exceeding two hundred ringgit for each day during
which the offence is continued after conviction.

Revocation and transitional provisions
39. (1)  The following By-laws are revoked:

  (a) Labuan Municipal Council (Hairdressers) By -Laws 1968
[G.N.L. 10 of 1968]; and

  (b) Labuan Municipal Council (Laundries) By -Laws 1968
[G.N.L. 13 of 1968].

(2) Any licence issued or approval granted under the revoked By -laws before
the coming into operation of thes e By-laws shall continue in full force until the licence
expires, is amended, suspended or cancelled, or the approval expires or is revoked
under the revoked By -laws, for which purpose only  the revoked By-laws shall continue
to be in full force and effect.

(3) Any proceedings pending or commenced under the revoked By -laws
before the coming into operation of these By -laws shall be continued and concluded
under the revoked By-laws as if these By-laws has not been made.
